confirmed.title: Same real payment posts twice: charge.succeeded + payment_intent.succeeded both handled
confirmed.claim: A single PaymentIntent-based card payment emits BOTH charge.succeeded (object ch_...) and payment_intent.succeeded (object pi_...). Both types are in HANDLED_EVENT_TYPES and both map to the identical posting (DR stripe_balance net, DR processing_fees, CR revenue gross). Neither dedupe key catches the pair: event.ids differ, and (event_type, object_id) differs on BOTH components â€” ('charge.succeeded','ch_1') vs ('payment_intent.succeeded','pi_1'). The transactions-table constraints (dedupe_event, dedupe_object, uuid5-of-event.id pkey) all key on the event, not the underlying money movement, so both post. This is exactly the double-count the brief's Â§4.3 single mapping row (charge.succeeded / payment_intent.succeeded share one row) and Â§5.3 'subscribe to only the event types you handle' exist to prevent. The books still balance (conservation invariant holds), so no test or trigger fires â€” but the ledger records twice the money that moved, which the reconciler will report as drift on every PI payment. Empirically confirmed: delivering both events for one $10.00/59c-fee payment yields revenue=2000, processing_fees=118, stripe_balance=1882; ingest answered 'queued' to both and the worker returned 'posted' twice. No test delivers both event types for the same payment, which is why 104 green tests miss it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Customer pays $10.00 via PaymentIntents (the normal Stripe flow). Stripe delivers evt_A charge.succeeded(ch_1) and evt_B payment_intent.succeeded(pi_1, latest_charge=ch_1). Both pass ingest dedupe, both enqueue, both post. Ledger: revenue 2000, stripe_balance 1882, fees 118 for a single 1000-minor-unit payment â€” every real PI payment is double-counted, with no fault injection required.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Handle exactly one of the two payment events (drop payment_intent.succeeded from HANDLED_EVENT_TYPES and from the webhook endpoint's enabled_events, per Â§5.3 subscribe-only), or normalize the money-movement identity before posting: for payment_intent.succeeded resolve latest_charge and use the charge id as stripe_object_id under a normalized event_type (e.g. 'payment') so the dedupe_object constraint collides with the charge.succeeded posting. Add an integration test that delivers both events for one payment and asserts exactly one transaction.
confirmed.verifier_reasoning: The finding is real, reachable, and empirically confirmed end-to-end. Code reading: HANDLED_EVENT_TYPES (src/ledgerproof/worker/handlers.py:25-34) includes both charge.succeeded and payment_intent.succeeded; build_transaction (src/ledgerproof/stripe_io/mapping.py:117-122) maps both to the identical DR stripe_balance(net)/DR processing_fees(fee)/CR revenue(gross) posting; the three DB defenses (transactions_pkey = uuid5 of event.id, dedupe_event = UNIQUE(stripe_event_id), dedupe_object = UNIQUE(event_type, stripe_object_id)) all key on event identity, and the cross-type pair differs on every component (evt_A vs evt_B, charge.succeeded/ch_1 vs payment_intent.succeeded/pi_1). No filter anywhere suppresses one of the pair; the ingest app enqueues any signature-valid event and its docstring states the endpoint subscribes to exactly the worker's handled types, so a real deployment receives both events for every normal PaymentIntents card payment â€” no fault injection required. Empirical run against a fresh migrated Postgres scratch DB using the real Deduper and handle_event: both events returned new=True at ingest, both returned 'posted' at the worker, two transactions rows landed, and balances read revenue=2000, processing_fees=118, stripe_balance=1882 for a single 1000-minor-unit payment â€” exactly double, matching the reviewer's numbers. The per-transaction and global conservation invariants hold (both sides doubled), so no trigger or test fires; FINDINGS.md is empty and no test delivers both event types for one payment, confirming the gap is unrecorded and untested. This contradicts the brief's correctness thesis (Â§0: never create money; Â§4.3: one mapping row for the pair because they are one money movement) even though the internal invariant is silent â€” the ledger records twice the money that actually moved, which the reconciler would report as drift on every PI payment.

confirmed.title: Recorded-but-never-enqueued event is lost forever; retry gets a false 'duplicate' 200
confirmed.claim: Deduper.check_and_record commits the stripe_events row (status 'queued') on its own connection BEFORE enqueue(event) runs. If enqueue raises (Redis blip, broker down) or the process dies between the two calls, the route returns 500/nothing, but the dedupe row is already durable. When Stripe retries the delivery, check_and_record hits UniqueViolation and ingest answers 200 {"status":"duplicate"} â€” telling Stripe to stop retrying an event that was never enqueued and never will be. Nothing in the repo ever re-enqueues or even reads stale 'queued' rows (grep: no sweeper, no consumer of status='queued'), so the event is silently and permanently dropped while every layer reported success. This breaks the at-least-once half of exactly-once: the RESPOND_500 fault plus one broker error converts a delivered, signed, acknowledged-as-duplicate event into a DROP that ingest itself caused. Empirically confirmed: first delivery with a raising enqueue â†’ 500 with the row committed as 'queued'; retry with a healthy queue â†’ 200 'duplicate', enqueued list empty.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Redis restarts for 5 seconds during a webhook burst. Delivery 1 of evt_X: dedupe INSERT commits, .delay() raises ConnectionError, ingest returns 500. Stripe retries evt_X a minute later: UniqueViolation â†’ 200 'duplicate' â†’ Stripe marks the event delivered and never sends it again. The charge never reaches the worker; stripe_events shows 'queued' forever; the ledger is short the money until (Phase-2+) reconciliation happens to notice.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Treat stripe_events as a transactional outbox: insert with status 'received', attempt enqueue, then flip to 'queued' only after .delay() succeeds; on the duplicate path, if the existing row is still 'received' (or 'queued' but stale), re-enqueue before answering 200 (process_event is idempotent, so a double enqueue is safe). Add a periodic sweeper that re-enqueues rows stuck in pre-processed states older than N minutes.

confirmed.title: Second partial refund on a charge is silently dropped by the (type, object_id) dedupe
confirmed.claim: charge.refunded fires once per refund with data.object = the charge, so two partial refunds produce two events with different event.ids but the same (charge.refunded, ch_x) pair. The dedupe_object constraint â€” designed for Stripe's 'two Event objects for the same state change' case â€” also fires for this genuinely new state change, and post_transaction classifies it as an idempotent DUPLICATE. Because mapping posts the cumulative obj['amount_refunded'] and the second event is discarded, the delta is never recorded. Verified empirically through handle_event: refund #1 (amount_refunded=3000) posted, refund #2 (amount_refunded=8000) returned 'duplicate'; refunds_contra ended at 3000 against a true refunded total of 8000, invariant green.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Merchant refunds $30 of a $100 charge, then later refunds another $50. Ledger records only the first $30; the second $50 movement vanishes with no error, no invariant break, and status 'processed' in the event log. Books overstate stripe_balance by 5000 minor units until the Phase-2 reconciler (not yet built) might notice.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Key refund transactions by the specific refund, not the charge: set stripe_object_id to the refund id (data.object.refunds.data[-1].id or the balance-transaction-linked refund object) and post the per-refund amount (delta of amount_refunded, or the individual refund's amount), so each refund is one dedupe-able transaction. Add a two-partial-refund test asserting refunds_contra equals the true cumulative refund.

Code reading confirms the mechanism: mapping.py:124 posts cumulative amount_refunded; the dedupe_object UNIQUE (event_type, stripe_object_id) constraint (and the ingest Deduper fast path on the same key) treats the second event as a replay; post.py maps that violation to PostOutcome.DUPLICATE; handlers.py marks the event 'processed' and returns 'duplicate' with no error. No compensating logic exists: the reconciler is a docstring stub and no test covers two refunds on one charge. The failure is real, reachable via ordinary Stripe delivery (no chaos needed), and silently loses a genuine money movement â€” the dedupe constraint over-fires beyond its documented 'same state change' justification. Major (not critical) because the internal conservation invariant holds and the planned Phase-2 reconciler could later detect (not prevent) the divergence.

confirmed.title: No enforcement that entry currency matches account currency; invariant is blind to it
confirmed.claim: entries.currency is free-form and nothing â€” schema, trigger, or post.py â€” ties it to the account's currency. The per-transaction trigger groups by entries.currency while account_balances/invariant.py group by accounts.currency, and nothing reconciles the two groupings. mapping.py:108,114 passes the Stripe event's currency into every entry while the account names are the hard-coded USD chart, so any non-USD event reaches this hole through the real write path. Verified empirically: post_transaction accepted DR stripe_balance / CR revenue for 100000 minor units with currency='EUR'; the USD-labeled stripe_balance moved by 100000 and invariant.check stayed ok=True â€” EUR cents silently counted as USD cents.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A legitimate EUR test charge (evt for a currency='eur' charge) flows through ingest -> worker -> post_transaction. The trigger passes (balanced within EUR), the view adds the EUR amount into USD balances at face value, and the money-conservation invariant â€” the project's thesis â€” reports ok. Balances are materially wrong (currencies conflated) with zero alarms; conversely, once a non-USD account exists, a txn like {DR usd_acct 1000 EUR / CR eur_acct 1000 EUR} passes the trigger yet breaks the measured invariant, producing phantom 'drift'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Enforce the match in the database: add UNIQUE (id, currency) on accounts and a composite FK on entries (account_id, currency) REFERENCES accounts (id, currency) (a follow-up migration; the brief's verbatim schema is a floor, not a ceiling â€” the repo already added TRUNCATE triggers beyond it). Also assert entry.currency == account.currency in post.py during the account lookup so the error is legible. Add a test posting a mismatched-currency entry and asserting rejection.

confirmed.title: Task exceptions are acked with no retry or failed-marking; transient faults drop events
confirmed.claim: process_event has no retry policy (no autoretry_for, no self.retry, no dead-letter), and task_acks_late acks the message even when the task raises (Celery's task_acks_on_failure_or_timeout defaults to True). So any transient failure â€” DB connection refused, post_transaction exhausting its 5 attempts on 40001 under CONCURRENT_DUPLICATE load, StripeError from the balance-transaction fetch, MissingFeeData with client=None â€” raises out of the task, the message is acked, and the event is never reprocessed. The stripe_events row stays 'queued' forever; the 'failed' status value in migrations/003's CHECK constraint is written by no code path anywhere, which is fossil evidence that the failure branch was never built. The docstring's safety claim ('redelivery after a crash is always safe â€” acks_late relies on exactly that') covers only SIGKILL-style worker loss (PARTIAL_WRITE); an ordinary raised exception â€” far more common under DELAY/RESPOND_500-style chaos â€” is a silent permanent drop with no marker for the reconciler to find.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Postgres restarts while the worker drains a backlog of 50 events. Each process_event call raises OperationalError on connect; Celery logs the failure, acks each message, and moves on. Fifty money-moving events are gone: not in the queue, not posted, rows stuck at 'queued', nothing marked 'failed', no alert. The ledger silently diverges from Stripe until manual reconciliation.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add bounded Celery retries with backoff for transient exceptions (autoretry_for covering psycopg.OperationalError, StripeError, serialization-exhaustion; retry_backoff=True, retry_jitter=True, max_retries~8), and a final failure handler (on_failure or a terminal except) that sets stripe_events.status='failed' so the reconciler/sweeper has a durable dead-letter signal to act on.
confirmed.verifier_reasoning: Confirmed, not refuted. Static verification: process_event (src/ledgerproof/worker/tasks.py) has no autoretry_for/self.retry/dead-letter; live-inspected Celery 5.6.3 config shows task_acks_late=True with task_acks_on_failure_or_timeout=True (default), so raised exceptions are acked; grep proves no code writes stripe_events status 'failed' (only migrations/003's CHECK lists it); recon/reconciler.py is an unimplemented docstring stub. Empirical end-to-end repro: recorded a charge.succeeded event as 'queued' via the real Deduper (ingest 200s, so Stripe never retries), ran the real worker against a failing DB â€” psycopg.OperationalError raised out of post_transaction, worker log shows 'raised unexpected: OperationalError', and Redis then showed LLEN celery=0 with the message absent from unacked (acked despite failure). After restarting the worker against the healthy DB, the task was never redelivered; the stripe_events row remained 'queued' and zero transactions were posted â€” the money-moving event permanently lost with no failure marker. Contrast demonstrated: a SIGKILL'd worker's message stayed in Redis unacked for redelivery, confirming the docstring's crash-safety claim covers only worker loss, not ordinary exceptions. This contradicts the brief's exactly-once-under-partial-failure thesis (Â§2, Â§5.3) and the module's own contract; the only overstatement in the claim is 'no marker for the reconciler to find' â€” the stuck 'queued' row is a findable marker, though nothing scans for it. Severity major (not critical): the DB-enforced money-conservation invariant is never violated and divergence is detectable in principle by the (future) reconciler, but accepted money-moving events are silently and permanently dropped on any transient fault.
